title: Daily Health Briefing
intro: Good morning! Today's digest leans on fresh human-trial data — the PEARL rapamycin results, new HIIT dosing guidance, the pelvic-floor biofeedback debate, a vitamin D / TP53 signal in HER2+ breast cancer, and where sleep meds and supplements actually fit. Sources are linked as chips below each section. Informational only — talk to a clinician before acting on anything.

sections.body:
This week is all new **human RCT** data — with the usual reminder that effects are modest and often sex-specific.

- **Rapamycin (PEARL trial).** The longest longevity RCT of low-dose weekly rapamycin (114 healthy adults 50–85, 48 weeks) found it **safe and well-tolerated**. It *missed* its primary endpoint (visceral fat), but **women on 10 mg/week gained significant lean tissue mass and reported less pain**, and 5 mg improved well-being. Exploratory — not proof of "anti-aging" — but reassuring on safety.
- **NAD+, done differently.** A 2026 *GeroScience* RCT of an oral reformulated NAD+ raised **intracellular** NAD ~53% vs placebo **without** changing plasma NAD — hinting that *where* NAD lands may matter more than blood levels.
- **Urolithin A.** An **NIH/NIA** trial (NCT06274749) testing 1 g/day on glucose metabolism in adults 55+ began recruiting **Aug 31, 2026**.

sections.body:
New 2026 reviews keep HIIT as a **time-efficient** option — and help pin down the dose.

- **Older women.** A 2026 systematic review & meta-analysis (*Frontiers in Physiology*) found HIIT improves **VO₂max, body composition, strength and physical function** in middle-aged and older women — often matching moderate cardio in roughly **40% less time**.
- **Dose matters.** A 2026 **network meta-analysis** in adults with obesity ranked **HIIT ≥75 min/week first** for cutting body-fat %, lowering waist-to-hip ratio, and raising VO₂max.
- **Pair it with strength.** A 12-week RCT in postmenopausal women (NCT07302191) found both HIIT and **concurrent** (aerobic + resistance) training improved glucose and lipid markers, but **concurrent training produced greater drops in weight, BMI and body-fat %**.

Bottom line: aim for **≥75 min/week** of real intervals, and **add resistance work** for body composition.

sections.body:
**Pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT)** remains the **first-line** treatment for stress urinary incontinence. This week's question: does adding **biofeedback** help?

- **Maybe — as a learning aid.** A 2026 sham-controlled RCT (60 women) found adding **EMG biofeedback — even *sham* feedback** — improved pelvic-floor activation, leak frequency and quality of life vs PFMT alone. The likely lesson: **supervised, structured practice** is what drives gains.
- **Big trials say it's optional.** The 600-woman **OPAL** multicentre RCT (*BMJ*, 2020) found **no meaningful difference** in incontinence severity at 24 months between PFMT with vs without EMG biofeedback; a meta-analysis agrees biofeedback isn't required routinely.

Takeaway: **consistent, correctly-performed PFMT matters most.** Biofeedback is a useful aid if you struggle to *isolate* the muscles — not a must-have. Confirm your technique with a clinician.

sections.topic: Alternative & Integrative Options — HER2+ / TP53 Breast Cancer
sections.body:
"Alternative" here means **evidence-based integrative care *alongside* standard HER2-targeted therapy — never instead of it.**

- **Vitamin D, with a TP53 twist.** A 2026 *Nutrients* study of curative-intent HER2+ patients found **correcting vitamin D deficiency tracked with better disease-free survival** (those who stayed deficient had ~**1.7× recurrence risk**). Because HER2+ tumors often carry **TP53 mutations**, it's notable that in a TP53-mutated subset of the **AMATERASU** trial, vitamin D showed **81% vs 31% 5-year relapse-free survival** (HR 0.27).
- **A mechanistic caution.** Older lab work shows **mutant p53 can bind the vitamin D receptor** and, in some contexts, shift vitamin D toward a *cell-protective* (anti-apoptotic) effect — so "more" isn't automatically better. This is **preclinical**.
- **Supplements ≠ free lunch.** A 2026 *Frontiers in Oncology* review flags **bioavailability limits and herb–drug interactions** for curcumin, quercetin and resveratrol.

Discuss any supplement with your **oncology team** before starting.

sections.body:
For restless, fragmented sleep, 2026 guidance keeps **behavioral therapy ahead of pills**.

- **The treatment hierarchy.** The **AASM's 2026** combination-therapy guideline ranks **CBT-I alone first**, combination (CBT-I + medication) second, and **medication alone last**. CBT-I often delivers durable improvement without drug risks.
- **Sleep hygiene isn't a cure by itself.** AASM conditionally recommends **against sleep hygiene as a *standalone* treatment** — pair good habits with the active pieces of CBT-I: a **fixed wake time**, **stimulus control** (bed = sleep only), and **sleep restriction**.
- **Supplements, honestly.** AASM has conditionally recommended **against melatonin, valerian and tryptophan** for chronic insomnia; melatonin's modest benefit is mostly in adults **55+** or **circadian** issues (jet lag, shift work). **Magnesium** evidence remains limited.

If fragmented sleep persists beyond a few weeks, ask a clinician to rule out **sleep apnea** and consider **CBT-I** (in-person or digital).
